'''Ali Yazdani''' (born 1967) is an American physicist who focuses on understanding new [[quantum phases]] of matter. He is currently the [[James Smith McDonnell|James S. McDonnell]] Distinguished University Professor<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 7, 2024 |title=Ali Yazdani named University Professor |url=https://www.princeton.edu/news/2024/02/07/ali-yazdani-named-university-professor |access-date=2024-07-25 |website=Princeton University |language=en}}</ref> at [[Princeton University]] and the co-director of the [https://quantum.princeton.edu/ Princeton Quantum Initiative].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schultz |first=Steven |date=September 12, 2023 |title=Princeton expands its commitment to research and education in quantum science and engineering |url=https://www.princeton.edu/news/2023/09/12/princeton-expands-its-commitment-research-and-education-quantum-science-and |access-date=2024-07-25 |website=Princeton University |language=en}}</ref> Yazdani is known for his research in advancing our understanding of emergent quantum phenomena by the application and development of high-resolution quantum microscopy techniques to directly visualize highly entangled quantum states of matter.

== Biography ==
Yazdani was born in 1967 and raised in [[Tehran]], Iran, prior to immigrating to California, USA. He received his BA in Physics with high honors from [[UC Berkeley]] in 1989, and his Ph.D. in Applied Physics from [[Stanford University]]. After working as a postdoctoral scientist at the International Business Machines Corporation ([[IBM]]) with [[Don Eigler]] he started his own independent research group at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]] before joining the Princeton University's Physics Department in 2005. In 2015, he was named the Class of 1909 Professor of Physics at Princeton and the Director of the [https://pccm.princeton.edu/ Princeton Center for Complex Materials] (PCCM), a  material research science and technology ([https://mrsec.org/ MRSEC]) center supported by the [[National Science Foundation]]. In 2024, he stepped down as PCCM director, became the co-director of Princeton Quantum Initiative and was named the James S. McDonnell Distinguished University Professor.

Yazdani has held visiting professorships at [[Stanford University|Stanford]] and at [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge University]] ([[Trinity College, Cambridge|Trinity College]]) in the UK and has been a Loeb Lecturer at [[Harvard University|Harvard]]. For his research accomplishments, Yazdani has been recognized by several awards and honors, including a Humboldt research award, and has been elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science|American Association for Advancement of Science]], and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]. In 2019, he was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]]. Together with [[J. C. Séamus Davis|Seamus Davis]], he was awarded the 2023 [[Oliver E. Buckley Condensed Matter Prize|Buckley Prize]] from the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oliver E. Buckley Condensed Matter Physics Prize |url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/buckley.cfm |access-date=2022-12-24 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Yazdani married [[Adele Goldberg (linguist)|Adele Goldberg]], currently a professor of psychology at Princeton, in 1994 and they have two children.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Couples at Princeton University |url=https://www.dailyprincetonian.com/article/2014/02/professor-couples |access-date=2022-02-02 |website=The Princetonian}}</ref>
